stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec on a multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature — high complexity involving real-time rendering, cross-platform sync, and CMS integration. openspec must elaborate requirements and define AC first; speckit then hardens with testability, security, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel feature — no preview-token handling, draft-content fetching, or real-time update mechanism exists in the codebase. The sole feasible attachment point is useContent (236 callers), the central hook all Contentstack content flows through. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs are written to our side of the boundary with explicit mock assumptions.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array, so all criteria are original to this review. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 form a token-presence triad (valid, absent, invalid) ensuring both happy path and edge cases are covered. (2) AC-4 addresses the real-time update requirement mentioned in openspec's note. (3) AC-5 is a security criterion preventing token leakage — critical because preview tokens grant access to unpublished content. (4) AC-6 and AC-7 tie back to the ContentstackLink and ContentCard files listed in technicalNotes, ensuring draft content flows through existing UI components correctly. (5) AC-8 is an error-boundary criterion for network failures during preview fetch. (6) AC-9 ensures the service layer correctly routes preview requests. (7) AC-10 covers the transition back from preview to normal mode, preventing stale draft data from persisting. CAVEAT: Without seeing the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, and contentCard.ts, some criteria may need adjustment once the existing interfaces, function signatures, and data shapes are inspected. For example, the 'refresh mechanism' in AC-4 may be polling, WebSocket, or Contentstack SDK-managed — the observable outcome (content updates without full reload) is the same regardless.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed meaningful, non-overlapping value. Openspec correctly identified the novel-feature context (no existing preview infrastructure), the primary attachment point (useContent with 236 callers), and the test-time constraint (Contentstack hosts unreachable, mock assumptions needed). Speckit then built a comprehensive AC set covering token triad, real-time updates, security, UI integration, error boundaries, and mode transitions — complementary to openspec's scoping work. However, two concerns warrant human review: (1) Speckit self-flagged that it created all 10 ACs without inspecting actual file contents (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, contentCard.ts), acknowledging criteria may need revision once interfaces and data shapes are verified. (2) There is a contradiction: speckit's notes state 'all criteria are original to this review' (i.e., it created 10 new ACs), yet acceptanceChanged is recorded as false. For a brownfield ticket with immutable ACs, this discrepancy needs reconciliation — either the ACs were not actually persisted, or the flag was incorrectly set.
